result.summary:
Scope test: this diff touches an admin settings-write flow for tenant branding (a tenant-data path per the dispatch instructions), so the gate was run for real rather than short-circuited on 'frontend-only'. No lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ file is touched (confirmed via git diff main --stat: only web/src/router.tsx, web/src/components/ui/__tests__/StatusBadge.test.tsx, test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/tenant-branding-applied.yaml modified, plus new files web/src/api/tenantSettings.ts, web/src/pages/admin/AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx, web/tests/e2e/pipelines/tenant-branding.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts, lib/letflow/design/req383-appearance-settings-screen.md, handoffs/WF02-REQ383-20260923/**). No new Ecto schema, migration, or API route handler is added -- REQ-382's PATCH /api/v1/tenant/settings endpoint was merged previously and is unmodified here.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation): NOT-APPLICABLE. No new/changed Ecto schema module or migration in this diff -- REQ-383 adds only a frontend client and screen consuming an already-shipped, already-INV-1-reviewed backend endpoint (REQ-382). The frontend never resolves or sends a tenant_id itself: confirmed by reading web/src/api/tenantSettings.ts in full -- patchBrandColorPrimary(primary) sends only {settings:{brand_colors:{primary}}} to /api/v1/tenant/settings, no tenant-id parameter anywhere in the URL, body, or headers, matching REQ-382's own design (tenant resolved server-side from conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id, per the module's own doc comment lines 3-8).

INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no new API response type; the response shape (TenantSettingsPatchResponse) is a pass-through display of REQ-382's already-server-authorised response, not re-filtered or re-exposed with new fields client-side.

INV-3 (sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- S5 not started, no scripting/plugin surface touched.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (live). Verified: grep for token/secret/password/Authorization literals in the new/changed files found none hardcoded. web/tests/e2e/pipelines/tenant-branding.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts's seedBrandColor(request, token, primary) takes token as a caller-supplied parameter (authHeaders(token)), not a literal. web/src/api/client.ts (the in-memory bearer-token holder) is unmodified -- confirmed via `git diff main -- web/src/api/client.ts` returning empty. PASS.

INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint; PATCH /api/v1/tenant/settings has no ID path parameter (S4 lookup-by-ID surface not implicated).

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES as the meta-invariant this handoff itself satisfies -- this handoff states explicit APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE verdicts with verification for each of INV-1..INV-8, matching its How-to-verify requirement. PASS.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no SQL, no lib/ or priv/repo/ file touched. (Confirmed no Repo.query hits possible since no Elixir file is in the diff.)

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES -- read AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx's onError handler in full: `const apiErr = err as ApiError; const detail = apiErr.details?.['detail']; setErrorMessage(typeof detail === 'string' ? detail : apiErr.message)`. This is a defensive typed-narrowing path (optional chaining + typeof guard), not a bare pattern match that can throw -- a malformed/absent details object safely falls through to apiErr.message rather than raising. No JSON.stringify, String(err), or raw details-object render found anywhere in the component (grep for JSON.stringify/String(err) in the new files returned no hits) -- confirms the error path cannot leak apiErr.details' full contents (which could include internal validation-engine detail) into the DOM; only the .detail string field or the top-level .message is ever rendered. PASS.

INV-9 (SSRF outbound URL validation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request derived from tenant-controlled input is added; this screen only calls Letflow's own already-validated API client.

Explicit checks requested in the dispatch, all verified against the real shipped files (not the design doc's claims):
- PLATFORM_ADMIN guard: confirmed present in AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx line 101 (`if (!session?.roles.includes('PLATFORM_ADMIN')) return <Navigate to="/instances" replace />`), placed after all hooks, byte-identical pattern to web/src/pages/admin/tenants/EditTenantPage.tsx line 116-117.
- Request-body shape closure (AC4): confirmed by reading both files -- tenantSettingsApi.patchBrandColorPrimary builds exactly one literal object `{ settings: { brand_colors: { primary } } }` typed as `satisfies TenantSettingsPatchBody`, no spread/dynamic-key/rest-param. AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx has exactly one form control (input type=color) bound to exactly one state variable (draftColor) and exactly one mutation call site (mutation.mutate(draftColor)). No code path can inject an out-of-scope key.
- Error-handler leak check: as under INV-8 above -- only .detail (string, type-guarded) or .message ever reaches the DOM; full ApiError.details object is never rendered or stringified.
- Token handling: web/src/api/client.ts unmodified (empty diff), in-memory-only token model unchanged, FNFR-06 intact.
- Tenant-scoping source: no tenant id is read, stored, or sent by the frontend anywhere in this diff; the endpoint resolves it server-side per REQ-382, unchanged here.

No BLOCKER found on any APPLIES invariant.
